A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TabPFN-TS and MoTM imputation benchmark. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original imputation benchmarks, probabilistic predictions, covariate experiments and runtime comparisons, including daily/weekly evaluations in Appendix C.

after.justification: V2 retains these empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, temporal-feature ablations, sparse-grid examples and SAITS tuning experiments.

M1.justification: The core TabPFNv2-based TabPFN-TS and pretrained-INR/ridge MoTM procedures remain unchanged. Alternative encodings are ablation controls; incomplete-covariate handling is discussed as possible extensions rather than changes to the evaluated main pipeline.

E1.justification: The 33 main univariate datasets, four daily/weekly datasets and three covariate datasets are retained. Figure 12 adds six-hourly-to-hourly reconstruction examples on Wind-France and PV-France, introducing a regular sparse-input scenario. Incomplete or asynchronous covariates are discussed but not evaluated.

E2.justification: V2 substantially expands the reported comparisons through Table 3: MOMENT's qualitative exclusion rationale becomes an explicit quantitative comparison, alongside newly included NuwaTS and cubic spline interpolation on eleven datasets. The original main-benchmark comparator set remains unchanged.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce five temporal-encoding configurations and a SAITS grid over model widths 128/256/512 and one to four layers, selected by validation MAE across four masking scenarios. V2 also documents NuwaTS evaluation using 96-step segments. These are additional protocols; the original benchmark settings remain intact.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained missingness and sampling-rate analyses, Appendix D tests dependence on temporal features, Appendix F examines SAITS tuning and accuracy–training-time sensitivity, and Figure 12 investigates sparse-grid reconstruction with covariates. These address substantial new robustness and methodological questions.

E5.justification: V2 adds Mean (Std) summaries to existing MAE, WQL and low-frequency results, plus shaded bands in Figure 13. These expand statistical reporting, but neither repeated-run counts nor seeds are supplied, and the bands' construction is unspecified.

E6.justification: Original per-dataset benchmark scores are unchanged, but v2 adds extensive competitor, feature-ablation, tuned-SAITS and sparse-grid results. Aggregate entries also change: low-frequency BRITS and Linear means move from 0.525 and 0.510 to 0.531 and 0.512 respectively, despite unchanged underlying rows (v1 Table 8; v2 Table 9).

T1.justification: Appendix D.1 adds explicit mathematical definitions of alternative temporal feature maps for the ablation, including daily-only, index-only and random-period encodings. The original feature map and WQL equations remain unchanged; no theorem, proof or theoretical guarantee is added.

C1.justification: The scientific claims in the abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain their scope: broad zero-shot imputation evaluation, covariate integration, and the TabPFN-TS accuracy versus MoTM efficiency trade-off. New experiments support these retained contributions.

C2.justification: V2 corrects the Figure 2 interpretation by explicitly identifying MoTM's third-place average rank and lack of significant difference from SAITS. It also adds substantive explanations of feature sensitivity, harmful covariates under sparse sampling, incomplete-covariate limitations and compute-dependent deployment choices.

D1.justification: V2 adds a paper-specific code-availability link, NuwaTS implementation access and its 96-step workaround, explicit ablation configurations, and selected SAITS hyperparameters. Existing pretrained-model sources, hardware disclosures and main training settings are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations concerning time-index modeling, ImputeINR, Imputeformer, temporal feature engineering, NuwaTS and TabPFN 2.5. It replaces the critical-difference-diagram citation with Demšar (2006). These broaden context without redefining the central novelty claim.

P1.justification: V2 revises the main-results discussion, removes redundant model descriptions from Appendix A.3, adds appendix subdivisions and acknowledgements, and updates author/publication information. Most existing prose and the main narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds four substantive tables covering additional baselines, feature ablations and SAITS tuning, plus two figures for sparse-grid examples and tuning sensitivity. Existing tables gain statistical summary rows, and figures and tables are relocated within the revised layout.

improvement.justification: Feature ablations and validation-selected SAITS tuning address important missing controls in v1, while additional competitors and covariate failure examples strengthen the benchmark's evidential support and applicability boundaries. Some added summaries require reconciliation, including TimeMixer++ at 0.677 in Table 6 versus 0.681 in Figure 1. These reporting problems limit precision but do not outweigh the substantial gains from testing previously unexamined explanations for the headline results.
